prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Kansas City Missouri for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t objectively name a single “best” dentist, but I can help you find the right implant provider in Kansas City, MO — and tell you how to choose one confidently.

Quick guidance
- For implant placement, look first at specialists: oral & maxillofacial surgeons and periodontists generally place implants most often. For the final crown/bridge/denture, a prosthodontist or an experienced restorative dentist should do the restoration.
- Priorities: clinical experience with the specific procedure you need (single implant vs full-arch/All-on-4), modern diagnostics (CBCT 3D imaging), digital treatment planning, clear cost/timeline estimates, good before/after case photos, and strong patient reviews.

What to check in any candidate
- Specialty and board certification (ABOMS for oral surgeons; American Board of Periodontology or ABP recognition for periodontists; American Board of Prosthodontics for prosthodontists).
- Years of implant experience and approximate number of implants placed.
- Types of implants/systems used and whether they guarantee restorations or offer warranties.
- Do they routinely use CBCT and guided/surgical planning?
- Who does each part of care (surgery vs crown) and how they coordinate.
- Sedation options and where surgery is performed (office vs hospital).
- Before/after photos and patient references or reviews.
- Cost breakdown (surgery, implant, abutment, crown, bone grafts if needed) and financing/insurance help.

Questions to ask at a consult
- How many implants of this type do you place per year?
- Are you board-certified and a member of AAOMS/AAID/ADA?
- Will you take a CBCT and show me the digital plan?
- What is your complication rate and how do you handle failures?
- Can I see before/after cases like mine? Who will restore my implant?
- Total expected cost and timeline from placement to final restoration.

Where to look for trusted providers
- AAOMS (oral surgeons) and AAID or ICOI (implant dentists) directories.
- American College of Prosthodontists directory for restorative specialists.
- Local hospital affiliations and dental school faculty listings.
- Google/Healthgrades/Yelp for patient reviews (read multiple sources).

If you’d like, I can:
- Search for highly rated implant specialists in Kansas City, MO (I’ll need permission to use web search or you can give your ZIP code or neighborhood for better local results).
- Narrow by procedure type (single tooth, multiple implants, All-on-4), insurance or budget, or by specialist type (oral surgeon, periodontist, prosthodontist).

Would you like me to look up top-rated implant providers in Kansas City now? If so, tell me your ZIP code or part of the city and what type of implant work you need.
